sentences.text: This animal belongs to the superorder Sauropterygia, a group of ancient marine reptiles.
Specimens measure approximately 2.75 meters in total length, though some estimates reach nearly 3 meters.
Its most striking feature is a hammer-shaped head with teeth arranged vertically along the jawline.
Scientists named the genus Atopodentatus, meaning "unusual toothed," because of its zipper-like dental arrangement.
It is the second known marine reptile to eat only algae, a rare diet for these creatures.
Researchers found a near-complete skeleton near Daaozi village in Yunnan, China, and formally described the type species Atopodentatus unicus in 2014.
Further fossil evidence from 2016 confirmed the animal possessed shovel-like jaws adapted for digging.
Its robust limbs and reduced neck suggest it was semi-aquatic, likely using its chisel-shaped teeth to root through seabed sediment.
Evidence indicates this reptile fed on algae found on the ocean floor.
This basal marine reptile lived during the early Middle Triassic period in Luoping, southwestern China.
